Mundane

/mun-DAYN/ — rhymes with domain · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something that is mundane is very ordinary and unremarkable, part of everyday routine rather than exciting or unusual.

He enlivened mundane chores like dishwashing by inventing games.

Worked Example

Every morning she followed the same mundane routine: alarm clock, shower, toast, bus stop, office desk—unchanged for three years.

These activities are ordinary and part of everyday life, not exciting or unusual. 'Ordinary' fits, but mundane more precisely suggests this is routine daily existence that lacks excitement or any sense of distinction.

How Mundane Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

ordinary

ordinary: usual and average, nothing special

routine

routine: done regularly as standard procedure

humdrum

humdrum: boringly dull from constant repetition

Antonyms

extraordinary

extraordinary: far beyond the usual or expected

exotic

exotic: excitingly unusual, as if from far away

How Strong Is It? — extraordinary → ordinary → routine → mundane

extraordinary vs. mundane

extraordinary vs. mundane: Extraordinary is the opposite end of the scale from mundane: an extraordinary event amazes everyone, while a mundane one is too ordinary to notice.

ordinary vs. mundane

ordinary vs. mundane: Ordinary is weaker than mundane; ordinary just means usual, while mundane adds a shade of dullness — everyday things so unremarkable they feel tedious.

routine vs. mundane

routine vs. mundane: Routine is close to mundane but milder: routine describes what is done regularly, while mundane stresses how flat and uninteresting those everyday things feel.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — mund

Root — mund: world (from Latin mundus) (Latin)

Suffix — -ane

Suffix — -ane: of, relating to (from Latin -anus) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin mundus meant 'the world,' so mundanus meant 'of this world' — everyday, worldly matters rather than heavenly ones. From 'belonging to the ordinary world,' mundane came to mean plain, everyday, and unexciting.

Use the root in a new word: mundanity

Use the root in a new word: mundanity: She joked that the meeting's sheer mundanity — a full hour spent discussing stapler orders — nearly put her to sleep; mundanity is the noun for the everyday dullness that mundane describes.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral

Mundane is the word when you want to emphasize that something is unremarkably ordinary and lacks excitement as part of routine daily life. For something that's just average or normal, 'ordinary' works fine; for something actively dull or tedious, 'tedious' might be more precise.
